entries.test: Public evaluations and technical results showing whether the described errors are unavoidable limitations of generative models or correctable defects would test this claim.
entries.note: He asserts an inherent technical limitation, not merely that current models make errors.

entries.test: Public model documentation and reliability evaluations would test whether prediction from dataset tags causes an unavoidable inability to eliminate hallucinations or operate reliably.
entries.note: The central claim explains an alleged inherent limitation. 'Might be able to do well' does not soften the categorical impossibility claim.
The claim attributes an internal assessment to AI companies; observable product errors cannot establish what they privately underestimate.
He explains the alleged lack of understanding through a lack of knowledge. No shared criterion distinguishes his meaning of knowledge from demonstrated model competence.

entries.test: Public audience studies and reception of films, shows, or commercials assembled from inconsistent AI clips would test whether even small errors make them unwatchable.
entries.note: The asserted universal audience reaction makes this empirically testable despite the evaluative word 'watchable.'
Calling this capability the 'greatest threat' ranks harms without a common standard.

entries.test: Documented sustained replacement of workers by generative AI and public outcomes of replacement experiments would test the claimed inevitable failure.
entries.note: The entry combines an 'inevitable outcome' forecast with a retrospective assertion about experiments.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and deployed applications available at publication would show whether practical outputs supported claims of comprehensive automation.
entries.note: This concerns the evidence available in February 2024, rather than a categorical prediction against future automation.

entries.test: Public timed studies of business-copy production with contemporaneous ChatGPT, including required editing, would test whether substantial time savings were possible.
entries.note: The word 'always' creates a testable universal claim about editing requirements.

entries.test: Public output collections from contemporaneous image models across varied prompts would test their visual diversity, usability, and recurring detail errors.
entries.note: The qualification 'kind of' remains intact; the claim still describes observable output characteristics.
The question and subsequent answer express doubt, rather than a firm prediction that the outcome cannot occur.
'I don't argue it will' withholds support and conveys doubt; 'does not expect' strengthens that into a negative expectation.

entries.test: Public longitudinal capability and accuracy evaluations would test whether generative AI was approaching a performance ceiling in February 2024.
entries.note: 'I believe' introduces his asserted assessment rather than an explicit probability.

entries.test: Public evidence of an AI expectations collapse followed by severe industry-wide losses, failures, or contraction attributable to it would test the forecast.
entries.note: The plain reading is a broad tech downturn triggered by disillusionment with AI; no deadline is stated.
The central judgment is that these companies should not have survived their product limitations.

entries.test: Public financial reporting and compute-cost disclosures for generative AI products at publication would establish their profitability and resource demands.
entries.note: 'Likely' qualifies his explanation for the stories' omission, while the product's unprofitability is asserted here and elsewhere.

entries.test: Public gross-margin and financial statements for AI model providers and conventional software firms would test the claimed disparity in retained revenue after direct costs.
entries.note: The normalization silently repairs 'as actual revenue' into 'keep far less of their money'; the source conflates revenue with money retained after costs.

entries.test: Public financing commitments, liquidity disclosures, and cloud partnership terms would test whether their strategic role insulated OpenAI and Anthropic from business failure at publication.
entries.note: The surrounding financial discussion gives 'at risk' a plain business-survival meaning despite the snake metaphor.

entries.test: Public investment agreements, cloud-spending commitments, and revenue disclosures would establish whether the investments obligated recipients to buy the investors' services.
entries.note: The claim explains how investments generate guaranteed customer revenue.

entries.test: Public hosting arrangements and cloud billing terms would establish whether every ChatGPT or Claude interaction generated revenue for a major technology provider.
entries.note: The 'on some level' qualification allows indirect revenue but retains the universal scope.
The central assertion concerns investors' motives. The separate preferred-vendor assertion could be checked against public agreements.
'Essential' and 'killer apps' supply no shared threshold for distinguishing useful applications from qualifying ones.
He reports his own difficulty identifying achievements; public examples cannot establish whether he personally struggles to identify them.
This is an evaluative comparison of hype cycles.

entries.test: Public industry revenue, operating-cost, financing, and resource-consumption data at publication would test whether commercial activity supported AI's financial and infrastructure demands.
entries.note: The surrounding profitability discussion gives 'sustain' a concrete economic reading.

entries.test: Public lifecycle assessments comparing AI's additional electricity-related environmental costs with its resulting environmental benefits would test the asserted net harm.
entries.note: 'Impossible to argue' emphasizes a substantive environmental claim rather than literally predicting what people can argue.

entries.test: Public customer-revenue and financing data following a downturn among AI application startups would show whether OpenAI and Anthropic lost their sole substantive revenue stream and became more dependent on big tech.
entries.note: The claim specifies a trigger but no deadline.
'Suggests' presents the worsening-loss prediction as an inference rather than a firm commitment. Revenue growth is its stated condition.
This expresses alarm and condemnation without a distinct, specified outcome to grade.
